abstract:
PURPOSE
To develop a mechanistic model which describes and predicts radiation response after combined DNA damage repair (DDR) interference and particle radiotherapy.


METHODS
The heterogeneous dose distributions of protons and 4He ions are implemented into the "XXX" (MODELX). Predictions for monoenergetic and mixed fields over clinically relevant dose and linear energy transfer (LET) range are compared to experimental in vitro survival data as well as the data available in the literature, including different cell lines and DDR interferences. Ultimately, MODELX predictions were investigated in a patient plan.


RESULTS
MODELX accurately predicts survival of cell lines with and without DDR interference (DDRi) in clinical settings of ion beam therapy based only on 3 parameters derived from photon data. With increasing dose or LET the radiosensitizing effect of DDRi reduces, resulting in diminished relative biological effect (RBE) of ion beam radiation for cells subjected to DDRi in comparison to cells which are not. Similar trends were observed in patient plan recalculations, however this analysis also suggests that DDRi+particle radiotherapy may better preserve the therapeutic window in comparison to DDRi+ photon radiotherapy.


CONCLUSION
The presented framework represents the first mechanistic model of combined DDRi and particle radiotherapy comprehensively benchmarked in clinically relevant scenarios and a step towards more personalized treatment. It reveals potential differences between DDRi+photon radiotherapy versus DDRi+particle radiotherapy, which have not been described so far. MODELX could aid the appraisal of clinical viability of combined administration of radiosensitizing drugs and charged particle therapy as well as the identification of patients with known DDR deficiencies in the tumor who might benefit from therapy with light ions, freeing limited capacities at heavy ion therapy centers.
